chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:
The pilgrim cuts off the Talbiyya on the Day of Arafah at the decline of the sun.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The Talbiyya (the ritual declaration of 'Here I am, O God')

ai.seo_question: When does a pilgrim stop reciting Talbiyya during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise moment for terminating the Talbiyya, marking the transition from the state of Ihram to the specific rituals of the Day of Arafah. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the importance of adhering to the Prophet's and Imams' guidance on the temporal boundaries of Hajj rites, ensuring the pilgrim's actions align with the Sunnah. The cessation at Zawal signifies the completion of the preparatory phase and the beginning of the core supplication and standing at Arafah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The pilgrim would cut off the Talbiyya on the Day of Arafaat at the (start of the) decline of the sun’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
People performing al-Hajj on the day of ‘Arafah, must stop saying Talbiyah at Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime).”’
